correctness.rationale: Direct case analysis reduces every orbit to the positive x-axis or zero. For x≤0 the image is on the axis and a negative axis point goes positive next. For x>0 put s=y−bx. If s≤0 then F²=(−as−dx,0); if s>0 then F²=(−bs−dx,−ds) has strictly negative first coordinate and F³=((ab−d)s+adx,0). Thus entrance takes at most four steps, including b=0 and the switching line. From (r,0), F=(−br,−dr) and F²=((ab−d)r,0). This gives a positive return after 2 steps for d<ab, extinction after 2 for d=ab, and a positive return after 3 with multiplier a(d−ab) otherwise. Uniform bounds on the finitely many transient and within-return branch products turn return contraction into global exponential stability; an available contraction rate is κ^(1/ℓ) for 0<κ<1. The neutral multipliers give primitive cycles and every nonzero periodic point must visit the positive axis, so this list is exhaustive. The lower equality is allowed only at ab>1. A multiplier greater than one forces unbounded return radii unless the orbit reaches zero. At d=ab>0 the s>0 third iterate is already positive, shortening universal entrance to three; F⁵ is then zero. At z=(1,b/2), F²=(−ab/2,0), F³=(a²b/2,0), and F⁴=(−a²b²/2,−a³b/2) is nonzero. At (2,1,2) the right polynomial is λ²+λ+2 and the left spectrum is {−2,0}, confirming the example. Independent rational spot checks iterated the displayed piecewise rule on an integer grid for (2,1,2) and checked representative ray returns; the analytical argument supplies all quantifiers.
residual_risks: Only the zero-offset, zero-left-determinant family with the stated trace signs and positive right determinant is assessed; the argument does not establish perturbation robustness.
